packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-08 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (first reader)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE STATEMENT
- Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of the work or author before or during this reading. I do not name one here.
- Beyond the stated rules: the script in image-002 lies sideways and in image-003/004/005 upside down. To read it I made rotated and cropped working copies of image-002..005 in a private scratch directory (no enhancement other than rotation, cropping and 2x enlargement of one narrow strip) and viewed those copies as well as the originals. I opened nothing else (no packet.json, no web, no search).

LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)
- image-001 (overview): spine of a printed book with the covering removed, seen beside a ruler and colour chart; three parchment pieces of manuscript waste are pasted across the spine as linings, separated by two sewing supports wrapped with thread, with endband tie-downs at top and bottom.
  * Upper piece (tile image-002): script runs vertically in the photograph (line tops toward the right of the image). One column fragment, c. 22 short lines; the lower-left part is a separate overlapping or folded flap with 5-6 more lines.
  * Middle piece (tiles image-003, image-004) and lower piece (image-005): script is upside down in the photograph. A wide column (c. 30+ lines visible over the two pieces) and, at the right of the photograph (= left when turned upright), a narrow strip holding the line-ENDS of a neighbouring column. Middle and lower piece look like the same hand and ruling; whether text is continuous across the sewing support cannot be confirmed (1-2 lines are hidden under each support).
  * Outer-margin note beside the wide column (photograph left edge of image-003, about a third down): a large letter (A or N?) with a small superscript sign, then "xxxi" (?) and a third short line "t..ne"(?). Tentatively a marginal reference/number; not secure.
- No rubric, running title, coloured initial or underlining is visible. Small superscript corrections/insertions occur in the wide column (noted below). Question-style openings ("2o quero ...", "Rn(de)o ...") are visible in the wide column: OBSERVATION. That this is a questions-and-responses text on confession is a TENTATIVE interpretation from those words only.
- image-006 / image-007: a different photograph - the same or another volume seen from the head, a parchment lining visible inside the hollow of the spine, script upright, larger and blacker, c. 13 lines, left edge hidden under tie-downs. Not obviously the same hand as images 002-005 (rounder, heavier letter-forms) - tentative.
- image-008 / image-009: two identical, strongly out-of-focus views into a hollow spine; only scattered words legible.
- Small brown script, heavily abbreviated; the tight crops do not show any full page layout (number of columns per page unknown).

LINE-NUMBER CONVENTION
- image-002: lines run vertically; "L1" is the rightmost line of the photograph (= first line when turned 90 degrees anticlockwise), counting leftward.
- image-003/004/005: text is inverted; I number in READING order with the image turned 180 degrees, so "L1" is the line nearest the BOTTOM edge of the stored image. (Counting from the stored top would run backwards through the text.)
- image-007: lines counted from the top of the image.
- | marks the physical edge/cut of the strip; (..) = proposed expansion; ? after a word = uncertain reading.

SELECTED SPANS
A. image-002, the whole upper piece.
B. Wide column, in reading order image-005 -> image-004 -> image-003 (overlaps noted).
C. Narrow strip of line-ends beside B.
D. image-007 (image-006 is its overview).
E. image-008/009 (little).
Unread: text under the sewing supports and under the tie-down threads; most of the first two lines of image-005; the last line of image-002; marginal note only partly.

A. image-002 (upper piece; lines complete at neither end with certainty - right end is cut)

image-004 L7 : R(espo)n(de)o q(uod) sic . R(ati)o? e(st) q(uia) a(n)i(m)a? sing..? ..o? [superscript above: "gue"?] h(ab)e(t)? s(ed)? hi[c?]

   Margin beside image-003 L13-L15 (outer side): large "A"/"N"? with superscript; "xxxi"?; "t..ne"?.
Most secure sequences in span B: "lazarum suscitavit mandavit ap(osto)lis ut eum solve[..]"; "2o quero ... confessio"; "Rn(de)o"; "per sacerdotem absolvet(ur)"; "quero si peccator qui confitetur debeat de omnibus peccatis suis confiteri . Rn(de)o quod sic"; "propter mala opera sua displiceret"; "non offenderet eum et omnes suos"; "debeat confiteri omnia peccata"; "non fuisti absolutus"; "ne sacerdos revelet confessionem meam"; "Et arguo".

C. Narrow strip of line-ends of the neighbouring column (left of span B when upright; left side of every line is cut away)
image-005 (reading order): |..is? ..q(ue)? ..ua | ..r v(er)o? p(re)cep.. | ..u(m) e(st) . [..]bum? | ..(et)? p(ro)hib..uo? | ..o (con)..? pos.. | ..etia . R(espo)n(deo) q(uo)d | .. publicata? .

(These are single word-groups per line; no connected sense can be claimed.)

image-007 L14: [tops only, above the sewing support]
(The recurring word in L2, L5, L11 begins "hedi-" or "medi-" with an abbreviation stroke; I cannot decide between a form of "hereditas/hereditatio" and "meditatio". "ut valeat aliter non vale[at]" and "Et ideo hic dicitur quod si" and "non solum" are the most secure.)

E. image-008 = image-009 (identical frames, out of focus)
Legible only in the middle of the visible leaf, about lines 4-7 from its top:
 ? : ..mun..? hic? ..dic..re? videm(us)?
 ? : ad regule? pinguior? ..a
 ? : [..] g(e)n(er)alia? tene(r)i? p(otes)t? sin..
Everything else is blur. A focused retake is needed.

LIMITATIONS / REQUESTS
- All three spine linings are abraded, stained with paste and partly covered by threads; every line of span A is cut at the right, span C is cut at the left, and the wide column of span B may be cut at the left by a few letters in some lines.
- Text continuity between the lower piece (image-005) and the middle piece (image-004/003) is not established; nor is the relation of the upper piece (image-002), which is turned 90 degrees and has matter on profession/"matrimonii" rather than confession.
- Whether images 006-009 show the same host volume or the same manuscript as images 001-005 cannot be told from the images.
- Useful additions: raking-light or UV images of the spine linings; an upright, focused image of the inside of the hollow spine (image-008/009); a wider view of the marginal note beside image-003.
- This is an unverified image reading; uncertain words are marked and no gaps were filled from sense or from any edition.
